adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the token refresh request is now conditionally routed through `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` (so it may call `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and return that `fetch` Response). Immediately after, the code still does `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`, which (by type `RefreshTokenResp` and existing Lark refresh behavior) expects Lark’s proprietary refresh response shape. Unlike google/office365/zoom/salesforce, Lark does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to validate/normalize a minimal sync-endpoint response, so a flat `{access_token, expiry...}` sync response would not match `RefreshTokenResp` and would likely throw/break refresh when sync is enabled.
